correctness.rationale: Finite Birkhoff representation reduces the weak excluded-middle equation to a condition on each principal downset’s minimal points. The common-upper-bound graph on minima is connected inside each comparability component, yielding the exact count. For a defective component with \(s\) points and \(m\ge2\) minima, there are \(1+t\) satisfying ideals, where \(t\le2^{s-m}\); at least \(2^m-2\) distinct failing ideals give the sharp upper bound. Equality forces exactly two minima, an antichain of all remaining points, and both minima below every remaining point. Component multiplicativity extends the bound to all finite posets. Exact small-poset enumeration and explicit extremal-family calculations corroborate the proof.

value.rationale: Weak excluded middle defines the canonical intermediate logic \(\mathbf{KC}\). Existing gap classifications provide no fixed-complexity rate. The sharp exponential failure floor \(2/(2^{n-2}+3)\), exact count for every finite dual poset, and unique equality type give a substantive quantitative stability theorem, not a renamed yes/no validity criterion or an arbitrary finite slice. The number of join-irreducibles is the natural cardinality of the Birkhoff dual poset.
